cadence: weekly, Monday before the US open
method: Every Monday each open call is re-examined against the claims its note made. The numbers are computed from the record: where the call stands against what the note called for, how far the stop is, and a price-only range for where it can finish, drawn from the position's own recent volatility with no view assumed. The verdict is a judgment, stated with dated evidence: each claim the note relied on is re-measured and marked as holding or not, and the verdict has to follow from those marks. A broken thesis closes the call on the Scorecard from the review date. The return a note called for is written once and never changed.

latest.book_now: After this week's review the book still holds four calls: short wheat through the fund, long US natural gas, long the yen and long US energy stocks. Three reasons are fully in place; natural gas moves to weakened because oil jumped about 10% on the week while gas slipped, so the gap between them widened again instead of closing, and the gas fund gave back about half its gain. Highest conviction remains wheat, up about 9% on the short with two and a half weeks to run and funds still not buying back, followed by energy stocks, which gained about 5% in their first seven sessions as oil went through $100. Lowest conviction is the yen, four weeks in and flat, though Tokyo renewed its warnings on Thursday. A reader holding the calls changes nothing today; the thing to watch is whether natural gas follows oil higher or the fund short in gas starts to grow into a squeeze the other way.

book_risk.note: correlations are of daily mark changes over the trailing 63 sessions; exposure is the position's % move per 1% in equities or the dollar and per +10bp in the 10-year yield

calls.title: Oil carries a war premium. US natural gas carries none.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate: median front-month gas gain over three months after an oil-to-gas ratio reading at or above the 95th percentile (42 episodes since 2004)
calls.expected_basis: the gas fund's gain to Friday's close (about +4.8%) plus part of the base-rate catch-up, since the ratio is back at the 94th percentile with about 60% of the horizon left; trimmed for a gas price that has not yet responded to oil's move
calls.view_now: The gap between oil and gas is back near its extreme, which is the setup the note bought, but this week it widened from the oil side while gas drifted lower. The gas fund closed Friday at 10.66, about 5% above entry, down from about 9% midweek. We still expect gas to catch up over the seven weeks left, with the record fund short as fuel, but with less already in hand we expect a little less than last week.
calls.action_reason: The reason for the call is still in place and the stop is far away; the week argues for watching it, not cutting it. The review will close it if the ratio swings back toward oil-cheap or funds start buying their gas short back while gas falls.
calls.weakened_reason: Every condition still holds, but the week went against the way the note said the gap would close: oil rose about 10% while gas fell, the oil-to-gas gap widened back toward its extreme, and the gas fund gave back about half its gain (from about +9% to about +5%).

calls.title: The last buyers just showed up in wheat
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate between its one-month (−5.3%) and three-month (−6.6%) medians for a two-month horizon, taken as a short return
calls.expected_basis: the gain to Friday's close (about +9.4% on the short) less a little give-back, with no further drift added because the fund selling the note relied on is done
calls.view_now: Wheat slipped again to 660.5 and the fund the reader shorts closed Friday at 24.00, about 9% below entry. Funds have finished selling their record length and have not come back in. With two and a half weeks left and the target already passed, we expect the call to finish close to where it is, above what the note called for.
calls.action_reason: Driver intact, target passed and the stop far away. It runs to its early-November horizon; the review will close it early if funds start buying wheat back.

calls.title: The record yen rescue looks dead. So did the last three at exactly this point.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's target: 147 on dollar-yen by late January 2027, the median months-two-to-six move applied from 157.34, roughly +6% on the fund
calls.expected_basis: the note's months-two-to-six median move applied from Friday's 158.14, less the small loss so far (about -0.3%), cut by about two points because the move has not started four weeks in and the record rests on three episodes
calls.view_now: Four weeks in and flat, which is still what month two looked like in the prior campaigns. Tokyo renewed its warnings on Thursday when a hot US inflation report pushed the dollar toward 159, and the dollar fell back to 158 by Friday. We still expect the move, but with a little less time each week and only three prior episodes behind it, we expect somewhat less than the note called for.
calls.action_reason: The driver is in place, the authorities are still talking, and the stop is well away. The review will weaken the call if they step back from readiness to act or dollar-yen pushes toward 162 without a response.

calls.title: Yields and oil are surging together. Energy stocks gained after that in 7 of 8 cases.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's expected return: the average fund return over six months in the eight earlier cases, with the 10% weekly-close exit applied
calls.expected_basis: the note's base rate held, because every condition holds; the early gain (about +4.6% at Friday's close) is part of that path, and the narrower oil-above-$90 cases (+8.7% and +4.6%) argue against adding to it
calls.view_now: Oil went through $100 this week and the energy fund closed Friday at 68.24, about 5% above entry. Bond yields eased from 5.24% to 5.09% but remain far above the level that would undo the call. The two earlier cases with oil above $90 both made money but less than the average, so we still expect the call to pan out roughly as the note said, not better.
calls.action_reason: Every condition holds and the exit is about 14% below the market. The watch is bond yields: a slide toward 4.75% would weaken the call.
